about.title: Orland Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Orland is a small place, home to roughly 7,550 people, and when a family here loses someone suddenly the whole town tends to feel it. Public records for 2025 show 13 injury collisions in Orland, with 20 people hurt and no traffic deaths that year. Fatal losses in Glenn County do not follow a schedule, though, and they often trace back to causes beyond the roadway: a farm or packing-shed accident, a fall on someone else's property, a medical error, or a crash out on Rt 32 or along Walker Street on a Friday afternoon. Under California law, a wrongful death claim belongs first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then to certain dependents and heirs. It is a civil matter, entirely separate from anything the district attorney may pursue, and it generally must be filed within two years of the death, sooner if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Orland families with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless something is recovered.

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Respect for the two-year deadline
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, and the clock runs much shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Reaching out early protects options you may not know you have.

items.title: A full picture of what can be recovered
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include the financial support your loved one would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: Orland recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death claims are unusual here?
items.answer: Not at all. Traffic is only one source of these claims, and in a farming community like Orland many fatal incidents happen on job sites, in fields, on private property, or in medical settings. The 2025 figures also reflect a single year; families who lost someone on Walker Street, 6th Street, Rt 32, or South Street in other years still have rights under California law. What matters is whether another party's negligence caused the death.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges in Glenn County. Do we have to wait for that case to end?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that stands on its own, separate from any criminal prosecution. Your family can pursue it whether or not charges are filed, and regardless of how the criminal case turns out. Because the two-year deadline keeps running either way, it is wise not to wait.

items.question: My parent lived alone in Orland and I am an adult child. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: Children of the deceased are among those given first priority to file under California law, regardless of age or whether you lived together. If there is no surviving spouse or domestic partner, you and any siblings would typically share that standing. An independent attorney can review your specific family situation and explain what losses may be recoverable.
